<script type="application/json" id="pack-y2w13">{"year":2,"week":13,"id":"y2w13","title":"Applications of Proportion: Triangles, Algebra and Travel Graphs","subtitle":"Ratios in the angles and sides of triangles; the special 30°–60°–90° and 45°–45°–90° triangles; Pythagoras and the trigonometric ratios as ratios; similar triangles and shadows; ratio in algebra and mixtures; distance–time graphs, gradient as speed, average speed and meeting problems; and speed–time graphs for acceleration and distance.","family":"number","section":{"no":5,"name":"Ratios, Rates and Proportions","strand":"Number for Everyday Life","from":12,"to":14},"outcomes":["Share the angles of a triangle or polygon in a given ratio.","Use the side ratios of the special right triangles, Pythagoras' theorem and similar triangles.","Solve ratio problems in algebra and in mixtures.","Draw and interpret distance–time graphs, using the gradient as speed.","Find average speed, solve meeting problems, and use speed–time graphs for acceleration and distance."],"keywords":["angle ratio","special right triangle","Pythagoras' theorem","trigonometric ratio","similar triangles","scale factor","mixture","distance–time graph","travel graph","gradient","speed","stationary","average speed","displacement","speed–time graph","acceleration","deceleration","area under a graph"],"notes":[{"title":"Ratios in the angles of a triangle","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"The angles of a triangle add up to $180^\\circ$, so sharing $180^\\circ$ in a ratio gives the angles."},{"k":"fig","id":"w13-angles","caption":"Angles in the ratio $2:3:4$."},{"k":"p","text":"For a polygon with $n$ sides, the interior angles add up to $(n-2)\\times180^\\circ$; share that total instead."}],"figs":["w13-angles"]},{"title":"Special right triangles","blocks":[{"k":"fig","id":"w13-special","caption":"The side ratios of the two special right triangles."},{"k":"box","kind":"key","title":"Side ratios","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["**$30^\\circ$–$60^\\circ$–$90^\\circ$:** sides opposite the angles are in the ratio $1:\\sqrt3:2$. The shortest side is half the hypotenuse.","**$45^\\circ$–$45^\\circ$–$90^\\circ$:** sides are in the ratio $1:1:\\sqrt2$."]}]},{"k":"p","text":"These come from Pythagoras' theorem, $a^2+b^2=c^2$: for example $1^2+(\\sqrt3)^2=4=2^2$ and $1^2+1^2=(\\sqrt2)^2$."}],"figs":["w13-special"]},{"title":"Trigonometric ratios are ratios","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"In a right-angled triangle with angle $\\theta$:"},{"k":"math","tex":"\\sin\\theta=\\frac{\\text{opposite}}{\\text{hypotenuse}}\\qquad\\cos\\theta=\\frac{\\text{adjacent}}{\\text{hypotenuse}}\\qquad\\tan\\theta=\\frac{\\text{opposite}}{\\text{adjacent}}"},{"k":"p","text":"Because they are ratios, they depend only on the angle, not on the size of the triangle. From the special triangles: $\\sin30^\\circ=\\tfrac12$, $\\cos30^\\circ=\\tfrac{\\sqrt3}{2}$, $\\tan45^\\circ=1$."}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Similar triangles","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Triangles with the same angles are **similar**: their corresponding sides are in the **same ratio**. This lets us find heights we cannot measure, using shadows cast at the same time of day."},{"k":"fig","id":"w13-shadow","caption":"The sun's rays make equal angles, so the triangles are similar."}],"figs":["w13-shadow"]},{"title":"Ratio in algebra and mixtures","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"If $x:y=3:4$, write $x=3k$ and $y=4k$ and substitute. A **mixture** in the ratio $a:b:c$ has $a+b+c$ parts; keep the ratio fixed when scaling up."}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Distance–time graphs","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A **distance–time graph** (travel graph) shows distance on the vertical axis and time on the horizontal axis."},{"k":"box","kind":"key","title":"Reading a distance–time graph","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["**Gradient $=$ speed** $=\\dfrac{\\text{change in distance}}{\\text{change in time}}$.","A straight sloping line: **constant speed**. Steeper means faster.","A horizontal line: **stationary** (not moving).","A line sloping **down**: moving **back** towards the start.","A **curve** getting steeper: speeding up (accelerating); flattening: slowing down.","Two lines crossing: the two objects are at the **same place at the same time**."]}]},{"k":"fig","id":"w13-features","caption":"Each part of a travel graph tells a story."},{"k":"math","tex":"\\text{average speed}=\\frac{\\text{total distance travelled}}{\\text{total time taken}}"},{"k":"p","text":"Time spent stopped still counts in the total time."}],"figs":["w13-features"]},{"title":"Speed–time graphs","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"On a **speed–time graph**, the **gradient** is the **acceleration** (rate of change of speed, in m/s²), and the **area under the graph** is the **distance travelled**. A negative gradient is a **deceleration**."},{"k":"box","kind":"warn","title":"Which graph?","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"On a distance–time graph, the gradient gives speed and the area underneath has no useful meaning. On a speed–time graph, the gradient gives acceleration and the area gives distance."}]}],"figs":[]}],"examples":[{"title":"Angles in a ratio","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"The angles of a triangle are in the ratio $2:3:4$. Find them. What are the angles of a quadrilateral in the ratio $2:3:3:4$?"}],"steps":["Triangle: $2+3+4=9$ parts share $180^\\circ$, so 1 part $=20^\\circ$ (see the figure in the notes).","The angles are $40^\\circ$, $60^\\circ$ and $80^\\circ$.","Quadrilateral: angle sum $=360^\\circ$ and $2+3+3+4=12$ parts, so 1 part $=30^\\circ$.","The angles are $60^\\circ$, $90^\\circ$, $90^\\circ$ and $120^\\circ$."],"answer":"$40^\\circ,\\ 60^\\circ,\\ 80^\\circ$; $\\ 60^\\circ,\\ 90^\\circ,\\ 90^\\circ,\\ 120^\\circ$","figs":[]},{"title":"Special triangles and Pythagoras","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) In a $30^\\circ$–$60^\\circ$–$90^\\circ$ triangle the side opposite $30^\\circ$ is 5 cm. Find the other sides. (b) The sides of a right-angled triangle are in the ratio $3:4:5$ and its perimeter is 60 cm. Find the sides."}],"steps":["(a) Ratio $1:\\sqrt3:2$ with 1 part $=5$ cm: the hypotenuse is 10 cm and the other side is $5\\sqrt3\\approx8.66$ cm.","(b) $3+4+5=12$ parts $=60$ cm, so 1 part $=5$ cm: the sides are 15, 20 and 25 cm.","Check: $15^2+20^2=225+400=625=25^2$ ✓."],"answer":"(a) 10 cm and $5\\sqrt3$ cm (b) 15, 20, 25 cm","figs":[]},{"title":"Heights from shadows","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A building 20 m tall casts a 12 m shadow. At the same time a tree casts an 18 m shadow. How tall is the tree?"}],"steps":["The sun's rays meet the ground at the same angle, so the two triangles are similar (see the figure in the notes).","$\\dfrac{h}{18}=\\dfrac{20}{12}$.","$h=\\dfrac{20\\times18}{12}=30$ m."],"answer":"30 m","figs":[]},{"title":"Ratio in algebra and mixtures","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) If $x:y=3:4$, find $(2x+y):(x+3y)$. (b) Solve $(x+2):(x-1)=5:2$. (c) A painter mixes yellow and blue in the ratio $3:1$. How much blue goes with 12 L of yellow? (d) Purple is made from red, blue and white in the ratio $2:1:1$. How much of each is needed for 20 L?"}],"steps":["(a) Let $x=3k$, $y=4k$: $\\ (6k+4k):(3k+12k)=10:15=2:3$.","(b) $2(x+2)=5(x-1)$, so $2x+4=5x-5$ and $x=3$.","(c) 3 parts $=12$ L, so 1 part $=4$ L of blue.","(d) $2+1+1=4$ parts $=20$ L, so 1 part $=5$ L: red 10 L, blue 5 L, white 5 L."],"answer":"(a) $2:3$ (b) $x=3$ (c) 4 L (d) 10 L, 5 L, 5 L","figs":[]},{"title":"Reading a travel graph","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A cyclist rides 4 km east in 10 minutes, rests for 5 minutes, then rides 3 km back west in 15 minutes. Find the speed for each stage and the average speed."},{"k":"fig","id":"w13-cyclist","caption":"Distance from the start against time."}],"steps":["Stage 1: $\\dfrac{4\\text{ km}}{10\\text{ min}}=0.4$ km/min $=24$ km/h.","Stage 2: horizontal line, speed 0.","Stage 3: the line slopes down 3 km in 15 min: $0.2$ km/min $=12$ km/h, back towards the start.","Average speed $=\\dfrac{4+3}{30\\text{ min}}=\\dfrac{7}{0.5\\text{ h}}=14$ km/h. The cyclist ends 1 km east of the start."],"answer":"24 km/h, 0, 12 km/h; average 14 km/h","figs":["w13-cyclist"]},{"title":"Converting speeds","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) A runner covers 8 km in 40 minutes. Find the speed in km/h."}],"steps":["(a) 40 min $=\\tfrac23$ h, so speed $=8\\div\\tfrac23=12$ km/h.","$12$ km/h $=\\dfrac{12\\,000\\text{ m}}{3600\\text{ s}}\\approx3.33$ m/s.","(b) Gradient $=\\dfrac{45}{5}=9$ m/s; $\\ 9\\times3.6=32.4$ km/h."],"answer":"(a) 12 km/h $\\approx3.33$ m/s (b) 32.4 km/h","figs":[]},{"title":"When do they meet?","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Towns A and B are 25 km apart. When and where do they meet?"},{"k":"fig","id":"w13-meet","caption":"They meet where the two lines cross."}],"steps":["Let $t$ be hours after 8:00. Kofi's distance from A: $d=5t$.","Ama starts at 25 km and comes back towards A: $d=25-20(t-0.5)=35-20t$, for $t\\ge0.5$.","They meet when $5t=35-20t$: $\\ 25t=35$, so $t=1.4$ h $=1$ h 24 min.","Time 9:24; distance from A $=5\\times1.4=7$ km."],"answer":"At 9:24, 7 km from A","figs":["w13-meet"]},{"title":"Speed–time graphs","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A car speeds up steadily from rest to 20 m/s in 10 s. The perpendicular from one vertex to the opposite side bisects that side and that angle.","This gives two right-angled triangles, each with angles $30^\\circ$, $60^\\circ$ and $90^\\circ$, hypotenuse 2 and shortest side 1 (half of 2).","By Pythagoras, the height is $\\sqrt{2^2-1^2}=\\sqrt3$. So the sides opposite $30^\\circ$, $60^\\circ$ and $90^\\circ$ are $1$, $\\sqrt3$ and $2$."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"A train accelerates from rest to 30 m/s in 20 s, travels at 30 m/s for 60 s, then decelerates to rest in 15 s. <script type="application/json" id="pack-y2w14">{"year":2,"week":14,"id":"y2w14","title":"Financial Mathematics: Ratio, Rate and Proportion at Work","subtitle":"Percentages as ratios; sharing profits, land and estates; simple and compound interest; depreciation; VAT, levies and commission; currency exchange and purchasing power; utility bills and tiered tariffs; health calculations such as BMI and dosage; sports statistics; and direct, inverse and inverse-square variation.","family":"number","section":{"no":5,"name":"Ratios, Rates and Proportions","strand":"Number for Everyday Life","from":12,"to":14},"outcomes":["Use percentages, ratios and rates to solve budgeting, sharing and inheritance problems.","Calculate simple and compound interest and reducing-balance depreciation.","Work with VAT, levies, commission, exchange rates and utility tariffs.","Apply rates and ratios to health measures (BMI, dosage) and to sports statistics.","Recognise and solve direct, inverse and inverse-square variation problems."],"keywords":["percentage","budget","partnership","inheritance","principal","interest rate","simple interest","compound interest","depreciation","reducing balance","VAT","levy","commission","exchange rate","purchasing power","tariff","unit charge","service charge","BMI","dosage","success rate","direct variation","inverse variation"],"notes":[{"title":"Percentages are ratios","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A percentage is a ratio out of 100: $35\\%=\\dfrac{35}{100}=0.35$."},{"k":"ul","items":["**Percentage of an amount:** $35\\%$ of GH₵2000 $=0.35\\times2000=$ GH₵700.","**Multipliers:** an increase of $r\\%$ multiplies by $1+\\dfrac{r}{100}$; a decrease of $r\\%$ multiplies by $1-\\dfrac{r}{100}$.","**Reverse percentage:** if a price **after** a 15% increase is GH₵690, the original is $\\dfrac{690}{1.15}=$ GH₵600 (divide by the multiplier, do **not** take 15% off)."]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Sharing profits, land and estates","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Partnerships share profits in the ratio of what each partner invested or agreed. A will may give fixed fractions to some people and share the rest in a ratio. Work in stages: take out the fixed parts first, then share the remainder."}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Interest","blocks":[{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Simple and compound interest","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"For a principal $P$ at a rate of $r\\%$ per year for $n$ years:"},{"k":"math","tex":"\\text{simple interest } I=\\frac{P\\times r\\times n}{100}\\qquad A=P+I"},{"k":"math","tex":"\\text{compound amount } A=P\\left(1+\\frac{r}{100}\\right)^n"}]},{"k":"p","text":"**Simple interest** is paid on the original principal only, so it grows by the same amount each year. **Compound interest** is paid on the growing balance (\"interest on interest\"), so it grows faster."},{"k":"fig","id":"w14-interest","caption":"GH₵1000 at 10% a year: simple against compound interest."}],"figs":["w14-interest"]},{"title":"Depreciation","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Most equipment and vehicles lose value. With **reducing-balance** depreciation at $r\\%$ a year:"},{"k":"math","tex":"V=P\\left(1-\\frac{r}{100}\\right)^n"},{"k":"fig","id":"w14-dep","caption":"A car losing 20% of its value each year."}],"figs":["w14-dep"]},{"title":"Taxes, levies and commission","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["**VAT** (value added tax) is a percentage added to the price of goods and services. Price including VAT $=$ price $\\times\\left(1+\\dfrac{r}{100}\\right)$.","**Levies** are extra percentage charges set by government. For example, Ghana's E-Levy on electronic money transfers was introduced in 2022 and abolished in 2025.","**Commission** is a percentage charged for a service, such as changing money or selling property."]},{"k":"box","kind":"warn","title":"Rates change","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Tax rates, levies, exchange rates and tariffs change with each budget or market day. Always use the rate given in the question, and check the current rate in real life."}]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Exchange rates","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"An exchange rate is a rate between currencies: \"1 USD $=$ GH₵10.20\". To change money, multiply or divide by the rate, then deal with any commission. **Purchasing power** compares what the same item costs in different countries once prices are converted into the same currency."}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Utility bills","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Electricity and water are charged by the **unit** (kWh or m³), often with a **tiered tariff**: a lower rate for the first block of units and a higher rate after that, plus a fixed **service charge**."},{"k":"fig","id":"w14-tariff","caption":"A tiered electricity bill."}],"figs":["w14-tariff"]},{"title":"Health and sports","blocks":[{"k":"box","kind":"life","title":"Rates in health","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["**Body mass index:** $\\text{BMI}=\\dfrac{\\text{mass in kg}}{(\\text{height in m})^2}$. Adult categories: under 18.5 underweight; 18.5–24.9 normal; 25–29.9 overweight; 30 or more obese.","**Dosage:** a dose of $d$ mg per kg per day for a patient of mass $m$ kg is $d\\times m$ mg per day, split into equal doses.","**Drip rate:** volume $\\div$ time, in mL per hour."]},{"k":"p","text":"These are calculations for learning; real doses are always decided by health professionals."}]},{"k":"fig","id":"w14-bmi","caption":"BMI categories with three example values."},{"k":"p","text":"In sport, a **success rate** is $\\dfrac{\\text{successes}}{\\text{attempts}}$, often given as a decimal or a percentage; a **win ratio** compares wins with losses or with games played."}],"figs":["w14-bmi"]},{"title":"Variation","blocks":[{"k":"table","head":["Type","Equation","Example"],"rows":[["direct","$y=kx$","cost and quantity"],["inverse","$y=\\dfrac kx$","workers and days"],["inverse square","$y=\\dfrac{k}{x^2}$","force and distance"]]},{"k":"p","text":"Find $k$ from one pair of values, then use the equation."}],"figs":[]}],"examples":[{"title":"Budget percentages","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A family's monthly budget is GH₵2000: 40% for food, 30% for rent and transport, and 30% for other needs. How much goes to food? If the budget rises by 15%, what is the new food allowance (same percentages)?"}],"steps":["Food $=40\\%\\times2000=0.4\\times2000=$ GH₵800.","New budget $=2000\\times1.15=$ GH₵2300.","New food allowance $=0.4\\times2300=$ GH₵920 (also $800\\times1.15$)."],"answer":"GH₵800; then GH₵920","figs":[]},{"title":"Partnerships, land and estates","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Two partners share a profit of GH₵50 000 in the ratio $2:3$. (b) A farmer divides 120 ha between two sons in the ratio $3:2$. (c) An estate of GH₵120 000 gives the widow $\\tfrac14$ and shares the rest among three children in the ratio $3:2:1$. Find each share."}],"steps":["(a) 5 parts: 1 part $=$ GH₵10 000, so GH₵20 000 and GH₵30 000.","(b) 5 parts: 1 part $=24$ ha, so 72 ha and 48 ha.","(c) Widow: $\\tfrac14\\times120\\,000=$ GH₵30 000. Remainder GH₵90 000 in 6 parts of GH₵15 000.","Children: GH₵45 000, GH₵30 000 and GH₵15 000. Check: $30+45+30+15=120$ thousand ✓."],"answer":"(a) GH₵20 000, GH₵30 000 (b) 72 ha, 48 ha (c) GH₵30 000; GH₵45 000, GH₵30 000, GH₵15 000","figs":[]},{"title":"Simple and compound interest","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"GH₵5000 is invested at 12% a year for 3 years. Find the amount with (a) simple interest (b) compound interest."}],"steps":["(a) $I=\\dfrac{5000\\times12\\times3}{100}=$ GH₵1800, so $A=$ GH₵6800.","(b) $A=5000\\times1.12^3=5000\\times1.404928=$ GH₵7024.64.","Compound interest earns $7024.64-6800=$ GH₵224.64 more, because each year's interest also earns interest."],"answer":"(a) GH₵6800 (b) GH₵7024.64","figs":[]},{"title":"Depreciation","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A taxi bought for GH₵80 000 depreciates by 20% a year on the reducing balance. Find its value after 3 years and the total loss in value."}],"steps":["Multiplier $=1-0.20=0.8$.","$V=80\\,000\\times0.8^3=80\\,000\\times0.512=$ GH₵40 960 (year by year: 64 000, 51 200, 40 960).","Loss $=80\\,000-40\\,960=$ GH₵39 040, which is 48.8% of the price."],"answer":"GH₵40 960; loss GH₵39 040","figs":[]},{"title":"VAT and a levy","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Assume a VAT rate of 15%. (a) An item costs GH₵400 before VAT. Find the price with VAT. (b) A receipt shows GH₵690 including VAT. Find the price before VAT. (c) Under a 1% transfer levy, what is charged on a GH₵500 transfer?"}],"steps":["(a) $400\\times1.15=$ GH₵460.","(b) Divide by the multiplier: $\\dfrac{690}{1.15}=$ GH₵600 (VAT $=$ GH₵90).","(c) $1\\%\\times500=$ GH₵5. (Ghana's E-Levy worked like this before it was abolished in 2025.)"],"answer":"(a) GH₵460 (b) GH₵600 (c) GH₵5","figs":[]},{"title":"Exchanging money","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) At 1 USD $=$ GH₵10.20, how many cedis is 50 USD? (b) Changing 100 USD costs a 2% commission. What is the total cost in USD? (c) 1 USD $=132.5$ JPY. How many yen do you get for 200 USD?"}],"steps":["(a) $50\\times10.20=$ GH₵510.","(b) Commission $=2\\%\\times100=2$ USD, so the total is 102 USD.","(c) $200\\times132.5=26\\,500$ yen."],"answer":"(a) GH₵510 (b) 102 USD (c) 26 500 yen","figs":[]},{"title":"A utility bill","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A household uses 420 kWh in a month. The tariff is GH₵1.50 per kWh for the first 300 kWh and GH₵2.10 per kWh after that, plus a GH₵12 service charge. Find the bill and the average cost per kWh."}],"steps":["First 300 kWh: $300\\times1.50=$ GH₵450.","Remaining 120 kWh: $120\\times2.10=$ GH₵252.","Bill $=450+252+12=$ GH₵714 (see the figure in the notes).","Average cost $=\\dfrac{714}{420}=$ GH₵1.70 per kWh."],"answer":"GH₵714; GH₵1.70 per kWh","figs":[]},{"title":"BMI and dosage","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Find the BMI of a woman 1.65 m tall with mass 68 kg, and of a teacher 1.73 m tall with mass 82 kg, and state their categories. (b) A 70 kg patient is prescribed 25 mg/kg/day in 3 equal doses. Find each dose."}],"steps":["(a) Woman: $\\dfrac{68}{1.65^2}=\\dfrac{68}{2.7225}\\approx24.98$: normal, but very close to overweight.","Teacher: $\\dfrac{82}{1.73^2}=\\dfrac{82}{2.9929}\\approx27.4$: overweight.","(b) Daily dose $=25\\times70=1750$ mg; each dose $=\\dfrac{1750}{3}\\approx583$ mg."],"answer":"(a) 24.98 (normal), 27.4 (overweight) (b) about 583 mg","figs":[]},{"title":"Sports statistics","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) A footballer scores 3 of 5 penalties. Find the success rate. (b) A team wins 60 games and loses 40. Find the win ratio and winning percentage. (c) A basketball player makes 10 of 15 shots. Find the shooting percentage."}],"steps":["(a) $\\dfrac35=0.6$, that is 60%.","(b) Wins : losses $=60:40=3:2$; winning percentage $=\\dfrac{60}{100}=0.6=60\\%$.","(c) $\\dfrac{10}{15}\\approx0.667=66.7\\%$."],"answer":"(a) 0.6 (b) $3:2$, 60% (c) 66.7%","figs":[]},{"title":"Inverse-square variation","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"The force $F$ on an object varies inversely as the square of its distance $d$ from a source. $F=16$ N when $d=2$ m. Find $F$ when $d=4$ m."}],"steps":["$F=\\dfrac{k}{d^2}$, so $16=\\dfrac{k}{4}$ and $k=64$.","When $d=4$: $F=\\dfrac{64}{16}=4$ N.","Doubling the distance divides the force by $2^2=4$."],"answer":"4 N","figs":[]}],"summary":[{"title":"Financial mathematics","items":["Increase by $r\\%$: $\\times\\left(1+\\tfrac{r}{100}\\right)$; decrease: $\\times\\left(1-\\tfrac{r}{100}\\right)$; reverse: divide.","Simple interest $I=\\dfrac{Prn}{100}$; compound $A=P\\left(1+\\tfrac{r}{100}\\right)^n$.","Depreciation $V=P\\left(1-\\tfrac{r}{100}\\right)^n$.","Exchange: multiply or divide by the rate, then add commission.","Tiered tariff: charge each block at its own rate, then add the service charge.","BMI $=\\dfrac{\\text{kg}}{\\text{m}^2}$; variation $y=kx$, $y=\\dfrac kx$, $y=\\dfrac{k}{x^2}$."]}],"quiz":[{"q":"40% of GH₵2000 is","options":["GH₵800","GH₵80","GH₵1200","GH₵500"],"correct":0,"explain":"$0.4\\times2000$."},{"q":"The simple interest on GH₵1000 at 10% a year for 3 years is","options":["GH₵300","GH₵331","GH₵1300","GH₵30"],"correct":0,"explain":"$\\tfrac{1000\\times10\\times3}{100}$."},{"q":"GH₵1000 at 10% compound interest for 2 years amounts to","options":["GH₵1210","GH₵1200","GH₵1100","GH₵1020"],"correct":0,"explain":"$1000\\times1.1^2$."},{"q":"A machine worth GH₵10 000 depreciates by 10% a year. After 2 years it is worth","options":["GH₵8100","GH₵8000","GH₵9000","GH₵12 100"],"correct":0,"explain":"$10\\,000\\times0.9^2$."},{"q":"A price including 15% VAT is GH₵230. The price before VAT is","options":["GH₵200","GH₵195.50","GH₵215","GH₵264.50"],"correct":0,"explain":"$230\\div1.15$."},{"q":"Profit of GH₵900 shared in the ratio $4:5$ gives the smaller share as","options":["GH₵400","GH₵500","GH₵450","GH₵360"],"correct":0,"explain":"One part is GH₵100."},{"q":"At 1 EUR $=$ GH₵10.50, how many cedis is 50 EUR?","options":["GH₵525","GH₵4.76","GH₵60.50","GH₵52.50"],"correct":0,"explain":"$50\\times10.50$."},{"q":"A person of mass 72 kg and height 1.8 m has BMI","options":["about 22.2","40","about 26.7","129.6"],"correct":0,"explain":"$72\\div3.24$."},{"q":"A team wins 18 of 24 games. Its success rate is","options":["0.75","0.25","1.33","18"],"correct":0,"explain":"$18\\div24$."},{"q":"If $y\\propto\\dfrac{1}{x^2}$ and $x$ is doubled, then $y$ is","options":["divided by 4","halved","doubled","multiplied by 4"],"correct":0,"explain":"$\\tfrac{1}{(2x)^2}=\\tfrac14\\cdot\\tfrac1{x^2}$."}],"exercise":[{"q":"A footballer scores 3 penalties out of 5. Give the success rate as a decimal.","a":"0.6"},{"q":"A team wins 60 games and loses 40. Give the winning percentage as a decimal.","a":"0.6"},{"q":"Convert 200 USD to yen at 1 USD $=132.5$ JPY.","a":"26 500 yen"},{"q":"You change 50 EUR to cedis at 1 EUR $=$ GH₵10.50 with a 1.5% commission. Find the cedis received and the total cost in euros.","a":"GH₵525; total cost 50.75 EUR"},{"q":"Bread costs 5 EUR in France and 300 MXN in Mexico, and 1 EUR $=20$ MXN. Find the bill for 250 kWh.","a":"$20+7.50=$ GH₵27.50"},{"q":"Find the compound amount on GH₵2000 at 8% a year for 2 years.","a":"$2000\\times1.08^2=$ GH₵2332.80"},{"q":"A recipe uses 2 cups of flour for every 3 eggs. How much flour is needed for 6 eggs?","a":"4 cups"},{"q":"Is the distance travelled at constant speed directly or inversely proportional to the time?","a":"Directly: $d=vt$"}],"theory":[{"q":"Kwame borrows GH₵8000 for 2 years. Which loan is cheaper, and by how much?","steps":["A: $I=\\dfrac{8000\\times15\\times2}{100}=$ GH₵2400, so he repays GH₵10 400.","B: $A=8000\\times1.14^2=8000\\times1.2996=$ GH₵10 396.80.","B is cheaper by GH₵3.20. Over 2 years the lower rate just beats the compounding; over a longer period the compounding would make B more expensive. (Over 3 years: A costs GH₵11 600, B costs GH₵11 852.35.)"],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"A trader buys goods for GH₵2500 and marks them up by 40%. VAT at 15% is then added to the marked price. A customer pays with a 1% charge for a mobile money transfer. Find (a) the marked price (b) the price with VAT (c) the total the customer pays.","steps":["(a) $2500\\times1.40=$ GH₵3500.","(b) $3500\\times1.15=$ GH₵4025.","(c) Transfer charge $=1\\%\\times4025=$ GH₵40.25, so the customer pays GH₵4065.25.","Each percentage is applied to the amount from the stage before, so the overall multiplier is $1.40\\times1.15\\times1.01\\approx1.626$."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"A printer bought for GH₵12 000 depreciates by 25% a year. (a) Find its value after 3 years. (b) After how many whole years is it first worth less than GH₵3000? (c) Compare with straight-line depreciation of GH₵3000 a year.","steps":["(a) $12\\,000\\times0.75^3=$ GH₵5062.50.","(b) Year 4: $5062.50\\times0.75\\approx$ GH₵3796.88; year 5: about GH₵2847.66. So after **5 years** it is first below GH₵3000.","(c) Straight-line: $12\\,000-3000n$ reaches GH₵3000 after 3 years and zero after 4. Reducing balance loses more in the first year (GH₵3000 either way), then less each year, and never reaches zero."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"Explain how understanding a consumption rate (kWh per day) can help a family reduce its electricity bill. Illustrate with a fridge using 1.2 kWh a day and a tariff of GH₵1.80 per kWh.","steps":["A consumption rate shows how much energy each appliance uses per day, so the family can see which appliances cost the most and target them.","Fridge: $1.2\\times30=36$ kWh a month, costing $36\\times1.80=$ GH₵64.80. A more efficient fridge using 0.8 kWh a day would use 24 kWh and cost GH₵43.20, saving GH₵21.60 a month (GH₵259.20 a year).","With a tiered tariff, cutting use can also keep the household in the cheaper block, saving even more per unit."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"Classify each relationship as direct variation, inverse variation or neither, giving an equation where possible: (a) distance travelled at a constant speed and time (b) the time for a journey and the speed (c) the number of workers and days to finish a job (d) a taxi fare of GH₵10 plus GH₵2 per km and the distance.","steps":["(a) **Direct:** $d=vt$; doubling the time doubles the distance.","(b) **Inverse:** $t=\\dfrac{d}{v}$; doubling the speed halves the time.","(c) **Inverse:** days $=\\dfrac{k}{\\text{workers}}$, where $k$ is the number of worker-days.","(d) **Neither:** $F=10+2d$ is linear but does not pass through the origin; doubling the distance does not double the fare (5 km costs GH₵20, 10 km costs GH₵30)."],"answer":"","model":null}],"checklist":["I can use percentages and multipliers, including reverse percentages.","I can share profits, land and estates in given <script type="application/json" id="pack-y2w15">{"year":2,"week":15,"id":"y2w15","title":"Sequences and Series I: Patterns and Arithmetic Progressions","subtitle":"Sequences and series; patterns from plane figures (triangular, square and cube numbers, matchstick patterns, Fibonacci); arithmetic (linear) sequences and the nth term; finding the first term and common difference from two terms; testing whether a number is a term; the sum of an arithmetic series, sigma notation and finding the number of terms.","family":"algebra","section":{"no":6,"name":"Patterns: Sequences and Series","strand":"Algebraic Reasoning","from":15,"to":17},"outcomes":["Describe and continue patterns made from plane figures and find a rule for them.","Recognise an arithmetic progression (AP) and find its common difference.","Find and use the nth term $U_n=a+(n-1)d$, including from two given terms.","Find the sum of an arithmetic series using $S_n=\\tfrac n2[2a+(n-1)d]$ or $S_n=\\tfrac n2(a+l)$.","Solve problems that require the number of terms or the first term of an AP."],"keywords":["sequence","term","series","finite","infinite","pattern","triangular numbers","square numbers","cube numbers","Fibonacci sequence","arithmetic progression","linear sequence","common difference","nth term","general term","last term","arithmetic series","sum","sigma notation","arithmetic mean"],"notes":[{"title":"Sequences and series","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A **sequence** is an ordered list of numbers that follows a rule; each number is a **term**. We write $U_1$ for the first term, $U_2$ for the second, and $U_n$ for the **$n$th term** (the general term). A sequence may be **finite** (it stops) or **infinite** (it goes on for ever)."},{"k":"p","text":"A **series** is the **sum** of the terms of a sequence: the sequence $2,4,6,8$ gives the series $2+4+6+8=20$."},{"k":"box","kind":"life","title":"Patterns around us","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Patterns appear everywhere: the hexagonal cells of a honeycomb, the rings of a tree, the ripples on a pond, the spirals of a pineapple or a sunflower. Many of these spirals count in **Fibonacci numbers**: $1,1,2,3,5,8,13,\\dots$, where each term is the sum of the two before it ($U_{n}=U_{n-1}+U_{n-2}$)."}]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Patterns from figures","blocks":[{"k":"fig","id":"w15-figurate","caption":"Triangular, square and cube numbers."},{"k":"table","head":["Pattern","First terms","$n$th term"],"rows":[["triangular numbers","1, 3, 6, 10, 15, …","$\\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}$"],["square numbers","1, 4, 9, 16, 25, …","$n^2$"],["cube numbers","1, 8, 27, 64, 125, …","$n^3$"]]},{"k":"p","text":"A pattern that grows by the **same amount** each time gives a **linear** sequence."},{"k":"fig","id":"w15-matches","caption":"Each new square adds 3 matches."}],"figs":["w15-figurate","w15-matches"]},{"title":"Arithmetic progressions","blocks":[{"k":"box","kind":"definition","title":"Arithmetic progression (AP)","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"An **arithmetic progression** (linear sequence) is a sequence in which each term is found by **adding a fixed number** $d$, the **common difference**, to the term before:"},{"k":"math","tex":"a,\\ a+d,\\ a+2d,\\ a+3d,\\ \\dots\\qquad d=U_{n+1}-U_n"}]},{"k":"p","text":"The terms go up when $d>0$ and down when $d<0$. Because the first term has $0$ lots of $d$, the second $1$ lot, and so on:"},{"k":"math","tex":"U_n=a+(n-1)d"},{"k":"p","text":"This simplifies to $U_n=dn+(a-d)$: a **linear** expression in $n$. Plotted against $n$, the terms of an AP lie on a straight line with gradient $d$."},{"k":"fig","id":"w15-line","caption":"Terms of an AP lie on a straight line."},{"k":"box","kind":"tip","title":"Using the nth term","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["**Find a term:** substitute the value of $n$.","**Is $x$ a term?** Solve $U_n=x$; it is a term only if $n$ is a positive whole number.","**Given two terms:** write two equations, such as $a+2d=11$ and $a+7d=31$, and solve them simultaneously.","**Three terms in an AP:** the middle one is the mean of the other two, $b=\\dfrac{a+c}{2}$ (the **arithmetic mean**)."]}]}],"figs":["w15-line"]},{"title":"The sum of an arithmetic series","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Gauss is said to have added $1+2+\\dots+100$ in moments by pairing the first and last terms."},{"k":"fig","id":"w15-gauss","caption":"Writing the sum forwards and backwards."},{"k":"p","text":"Write $S_n=a+(a+d)+\\dots+l$ forwards and backwards and add: each of the $n$ columns adds to $a+l$, so $2S_n=n(a+l)$."},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Sum of an AP","blocks":[{"k":"math","tex":"S_n=\\frac n2\\big[2a+(n-1)d\\big]\\qquad\\text{or}\\qquad S_n=\\frac n2\\,(a+l)"},{"k":"p","text":"where $l=a+(n-1)d$ is the last term."}]}],"figs":["w15-gauss"]},{"title":"Sigma notation","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"$\\displaystyle\\sum_{r=1}^{n}U_r$ means \"add the terms $U_1$ to $U_n$\". For example $\\displaystyle\\sum_{r=1}^{5}(2r+1)=3+5+7+9+11=35$."}],"figs":[]}],"examples":[{"title":"Patterns from figures","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Find the 10th triangular number and the 10th square number. (b) Write the next three terms of the Fibonacci sequence $1,1,2,3,5,8,\\dots$ (c) Show that the sum of two consecutive triangular numbers is a square number."}],"steps":["(a) $T_{10}=\\dfrac{10\\times11}{2}=55$ and $10^2=100$.","(b) $5+8=13$, $8+13=21$, $13+21=34$.","(c) $T_{n-1}+T_n=\\dfrac{(n-1)n}{2}+\\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}=\\dfrac{n(2n)}{2}=n^2$. For example $6+10=16$."],"answer":"(a) 55, 100 (b) 13, 21, 34 (c) $T_{n-1}+T_n=n^2$","figs":[]},{"title":"A matchstick pattern","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Matchsticks make a row of squares: 4, 7, 10, 13, … matches. (a) Find the rule. (b) How many matches make 50 squares? (c) Which pattern uses 100 matches?"}],"steps":["(a) Each square adds 3 matches: $a=4$, $d=3$, so $U_n=4+3(n-1)=3n+1$.","(b) $U_{50}=3(50)+1=151$ matches.","(c) $3n+1=100$ gives $n=33$: the 33rd pattern."],"answer":"(a) $3n+1$ (b) 151 (c) $n=33$","figs":[]},{"title":"Finding the nth term","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Find the $n$th term of $2,5,8,\\dots$ and the 6th term. (b) Find the 15th term of $-3,-1,1,3,\\dots$"}],"steps":["(a) $a=2$, $d=3$: $\\ U_n=2+3(n-1)=3n-1$, so $U_6=17$.","(b) $a=-3$, $d=-1-(-3)=2$.","$U_{15}=-3+(15-1)(2)=-3+28=25$."],"answer":"(a) $3n-1$; 17 (b) 25","figs":[]},{"title":"Fractions in an AP","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) An AP has first term $\\tfrac12$ and 10th term 9. (b) Find the general term of $-\\tfrac12,\\ 2,\\ \\tfrac92,\\ \\dots$"}],"steps":["(a) $9=\\tfrac12+9d$, so $9d=\\tfrac{17}{2}$ and $d=\\tfrac{17}{18}$.","(b) $a=-\\tfrac12$ and $d=2-\\left(-\\tfrac12\\right)=\\tfrac52$.","$U_n=-\\tfrac12+\\tfrac52(n-1)=\\tfrac52n-3$."],"answer":"(a) $d=\\tfrac{17}{18}$ (b) $U_n=\\tfrac52n-3$","figs":[]},{"title":"Two terms given","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"The 3rd term of an AP is 11 and the 8th term is 31. Subtract: $5d=20$, so $d=4$ and $a=3$.","$U_n=3+4(n-1)=4n-1$.","(b) $4n-1=99$ gives $n=25$: 99 is the 25th term.","$4n-1=150$ gives $n=37.75$, not a whole number, so 150 is **not** a term."],"answer":"(a) $a=3$, $d=4$, $U_n=4n-1$ (b) yes ($n=25$); no","figs":[]},{"title":"Sums of APs","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Find the sum of the first 50 terms of $1,3,5,7,\\dots$ (b) Find $S_{10}$ for $3,7,11,\\dots$ (c) Evaluate $\\displaystyle\\sum_{r=1}^{20}(2r+3)$."}],"steps":["(a) $a=1$, $d=2$: $\\ S_{50}=\\tfrac{50}{2}[2+49(2)]=25\\times100=2500$.","(b) $a=3$, $d=4$: $\\ S_{10}=5[6+9(4)]=5\\times42=210$.","(c) The terms are $5,7,\\dots,43$: an AP with $n=20$, $a=5$, $l=43$, so the sum is $\\tfrac{20}{2}(5+43)=480$."],"answer":"(a) 2500 (b) 210 (c) 480","figs":[]},{"title":"Sum from the last term","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Find the sum of $1+3.5+6+8.5+\\dots+101$."}],"steps":["$a=1$, $d=2.5$, last term $l=101$.","Number of terms: $1+(n-1)(2.5)=101$, so $n-1=40$ and $n=41$.","$S_{41}=\\tfrac{41}{2}(1+101)=41\\times51=2091$."],"answer":"2091","figs":[]},{"title":"A condition on the sums","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"An AP has first term 3, and the sum of its first 8 terms is twice the sum of its first 5 terms. Divide: $r^2=\\tfrac49$, so $r=\\tfrac23$ or $r=-\\tfrac23$.","If $r=\\tfrac23$: $a=9\\div\\tfrac23=13.5$, giving $13.5,\\ 9,\\ 6,\\ 4,\\ \\dots$","If $r=-\\tfrac23$: $a=-13.5$, giving $-13.5,\\ 9,\\ -6,\\ 4,\\ \\dots$"],"answer":"$13.5, 9, 6, 4, \\dots$ or $-13.5, 9, -6, 4, \\dots$","figs":[]},{"title":"How many terms?","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"How many terms are there in (a) $2,4,8,\\dots,128$ (b) $3,6,12,\\dots,3072$?"}],"steps":["(a) $2\\times2^{n-1}=128$, so $2^{n-1}=64=2^6$ and $n=7$.","(b) $3\\times2^{n-1}=3072$, so $2^{n-1}=1024=2^{10}$ and $n=11$.","With logarithms: $n-1=\\dfrac{\\log1024}{\\log2}=10$ ✓."],"answer":"(a) 7 (b) 11","figs":[]},{"title":"The geometric mean","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"The numbers $x-2$, $x+1$ and $2x+2$ are consecutive terms of a GP. Find $x$ and the common ratio."}],"steps":["Middle term squared $=$ product of the outer terms: $(x+1)^2=(x-2)(2x+2)$.","$x^2+2x+1=2x^2-2x-4$, so $x^2-4x-5=0$ and $(x-5)(x+1)=0$.","$x=5$ gives $3,\\ 6,\\ 12$ with $r=2$. $\\ x=-1$ gives $-3,\\ 0,\\ 0$, which has no common ratio, so reject it."],"answer":"$x=5$, $r=2$","figs":[]},{"title":"Sums of GPs","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Find (a) the sum of the first 7 terms of $\\tfrac12,1,2,4,\\dots$ (b) $2+6+18+\\dots$ to 6 terms (c) the sum of the first 5 terms of the GP with $a=3$, $r=2$."}],"steps":["(a) $r=2$: $\\ S_7=\\dfrac{\\tfrac12(2^7-1)}{2-1}=\\tfrac12(127)=63.5$.","(b) $r=3$: $\\ S_6=\\dfrac{2(3^6-1)}{3-1}=729-1=728$.","(c) $S_5=\\dfrac{3(2^5-1)}{1}=93$."],"answer":"(a) 63.5 (b) 728 (c) 93","figs":[]},{"title":"Sums to infinity","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Find $\\tfrac12+\\tfrac14+\\tfrac18+\\tfrac1{16}+\\dots$ (b) Write $0.\\overline{27}=0.272727\\ldots$ as a fraction."}],"steps":["(a) $a=\\tfrac12$, $r=\\tfrac12$, $|r|<1$: $\\ S_\\infty=\\dfrac{1/2}{1-1/2}=1$ (see the square in the notes).","(b) $0.\\overline{27}=0.27+0.0027+\\dots$, a GP with $a=0.27$, $r=0.01$.","$S_\\infty=\\dfrac{0.27}{0.99}=\\dfrac{27}{99}=\\dfrac{3}{11}$."],"answer":"(a) 1 (b) $\\tfrac{3}{11}$","figs":[]},{"title":"A bouncing ball","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A ball is dropped from 10 m. Each bounce rises to $\\tfrac35$ of the height before. Find the height of the 4th bounce and the total distance the ball travels before it comes to rest."},{"k":"fig","id":"w16-bounce","caption":"The bounce heights form a GP with ratio 0.6."}],"steps":["Bounce heights: $6,\\ 3.6,\\ 2.16,\\ 1.296,\\ \\dots$ ($a=6$, $r=0.6$), so the 4th bounce is 1.296 m.","The ball falls 10 m, then goes **up and down** each bounce height.","Total $=10+2\\times\\dfrac{6}{1-0.6}=10+2\\times15=40$ m."],"answer":"1.296 m; 40 m","figs":["w16-bounce"]},{"title":"When does the sum pass 35?","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"How many terms of $4+3.6+3.24+\\dots$ are needed for the sum to exceed 35?"}],"steps":["$a=4$, $r=0.9$: $\\ S_n=\\dfrac{4(1-0.9^n)}{0.1}=40(1-0.9^n)$.","$40(1-0.9^n)>35$ gives $0.9^n<0.125$.","Take logs (log 0.9 is negative, so the inequality turns round): $n>\\dfrac{\\log0.125}{\\log0.9}\\approx19.7$.","So 20 terms are needed. Check: $S_{19}\\approx34.6$ and $S_{20}\\approx35.1$ ✓."],"answer":"20 terms","figs":[]}],"summary":[{"title":"Geometric progressions","items":["GP: multiply by the common ratio $r=\\dfrac{U_{n+1}}{U_n}$.","$U_n=ar^{n-1}$. Geometric mean: $b^2=ac$.","$S_n=\\dfrac{a(1-r^n)}{1-r}=\\dfrac{a(r^n-1)}{r-1}$.","$S_\\infty=\\dfrac{a}{1-r}$ only when $|r|<1$.","Use logarithms to find $n$ when the power is Find $r$.","a":"$\\tfrac{5}{1-r}=20$: $r=\\tfrac34$"}],"theory":[{"q":"Derive the formula $S_n=\\dfrac{a(1-r^n)}{1-r}$ for the sum of the first $n$ terms of a GP, and explain why it gives $S_\\infty=\\dfrac a{1-r}$ when $|r|<1$.","steps":["$S_n=a+ar+ar^2+\\dots+ar^{n-1}$ $rS_n=ar+ar^2+\\dots+ar^{n-1}+ar^n$","Subtracting, every term except $a$ and $ar^n$ cancels: $\\ S_n-rS_n=a-ar^n$, so $S_n(1-r)=a(1-r^n)$ and $S_n=\\frac{a(1-r^n)}{1-r}\\quad(r\\ne1).$","If $|r|<1$, then $r^n\\to0$ as $n$ grows (for example $0.5^{10}\\approx0.001$), so $S_n\\to\\dfrac{a}{1-r}$."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"The 2nd, 4th and 8th terms of an AP with first term 2 and non-zero common difference $d$ are consecutive terms of a GP. Find $d$ and the common ratio of the GP.","steps":["The terms are $2+d$, $2+3d$, $2+7d$. For a GP, $(2+3d)^2=(2+d)(2+7d)$.","$4+12d+9d^2=4+16d+7d^2$, so $2d^2=4d$ and $d(d-2)=0$. Since $d\\ne0$, $d=2$.","The terms are 4, 8, 16: a GP with common ratio **2**."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"Write $0.1\\overline{6}=0.1666\\ldots$ as a fraction by using an infinite GP.","steps":["$0.1\\overline{6}=0.1+0.06+0.006+0.0006+\\dots$","The part after 0.1 is a GP with $a=0.06$ and $r=0.1$: its sum is $\\dfrac{0.06}{0.9}=\\dfrac{1}{15}$.","So $0.1\\overline{6}=\\dfrac1{10}+\\dfrac1{15}=\\dfrac{3+2}{30}=\\dfrac16$. Check: $1\\div6=0.1666\\ldots$ ✓."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"Explain the difference between an AP and a GP, using the graph of each against $n$. Give one real situation modelled by each.","steps":["In an **AP** the same amount is **added** each time, so $U_n=a+(n-1)d$ is linear in $n$ and the points lie on a straight line. Example: a salary that rises by a fixed GH₵1500 every year.","In a **GP** the terms are **multiplied** by the same factor, so $U_n=ar^{n-1}$ is exponential: the points lie on a curve that rises faster and faster if $r>1$ (growth) or falls towards 0 if $0<r<1$ (decay). Example: money earning compound interest, or the value of a car depreciating by 20% a year."],"answer":"","model":null},{"q":"A GP has positive terms. The sum of the first two terms is 15 and the sum to infinity is 27. Find the first term and the common ratio.","steps":["$a+ar=15$ and $\\dfrac{a}{1-r}=27$, so $a=27(1-r)$.","Substitute: $27(1-r)(1+r)=15$, so $1-r^2=\\tfrac{15}{27}=\\tfrac59$ and $r^2=\\tfrac49$.","The terms are positive, so $r=\\tfrac23$ and $a=27\\times\\tfrac13=9$. The series is $9+6+4+\\dots$, and indeed $9+6=15$ ✓."],"answer":"","model":null}],"checklist":["I can find the common ratio and the $n$th term of a GP.","I can tell APs, GPs and other sequences The **growth factor** is $r=1+\\tfrac{p}{100}$ for an increase of $p\\%$, and $r=1-\\tfrac{p}{100}$ for a decrease.","Use the **$n$th term** for the amount **in** a particular step, and the **sum** for the **total** over several steps."]}]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Watch the counting","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"If a population starts at $P$ and grows by a factor $r$ each year, then after $n$ years it is $Pr^n$: the starting value is year 0, so \"after $n$ years\" is the term $U_{n+1}=ar^n$.
